description.en: Fifteen sketches for the home page. None of them are the home page.

chaines.en: The Boring Blog · lab
All fifteen
Home page
Thirty sketches, none of them the home page

Every idea here is isolated on its own page, with the knobs exposed, so it can be judged by turning it rather than by reading about it. Nothing in this directory is imported by the site — the sketches share the meadow’s vocabulary and none of its page.
The dots are effort: one is an afternoon, three has unknowns in it. A line in red means the hook is already written and sitting unused.
Round two — the page
the sheet as a designed object
The cursor
the pointer as an instrument
The loupe
The pointer is a printer's glass. What is under it resolves; what is not, does not.
Registration marks
Two hairlines across the whole sheet, with ticks. It snaps to whatever it can act on.
The ink is still wet
The pointer has weight, leaves a smear, and the smear dries.
The type
letters as a physical event
Letterpress impression
The display type is pressed INTO the sheet, and the ink spreads at the edge.
The red plate slips
Hover a heading and it comes apart into its ink plates, then registers again.
Type that focuses
Weight and optical size track how close you are, the way a lens finds a subject.
Type printed on the field
The headline drawn to a texture and handed to the shader, so the grass truly cuts it.
The blades already sample a texture; this is one more
The layout
the grid, admitted
The grid, admitted
Baseline, gutter, trim marks, folios. Press a key and the sheet shows its work.
The archive as a contact sheet
Every post as a frame on one plate, marked up in red chinagraph.
The measure tightens as you read
Not scroll-driven animation — scroll-driven LAYOUT. The column narrows, the margin fills.
The components
controls that are objects
The nav is a set of tabs
Index tabs down the edge of the sheet. The one you press comes forward.
Buttons that stamp
Press and the ink lands — slightly off-square, and never twice the same.
The Button already has a two-layer fill and a seam
Progress as an object
Not a bar. A ribbon down the gutter, and a stack of pages that thins.
The press
plates, registration, and the page turn
The page turn
The outgoing sheet lifts away. The new one was underneath the whole time.
View Transitions across the App Router
The plates register
Paper, then black, then red — each landing slightly off and snapping into place.
Round one — the field
what the meadow could do
The light
the sun, the sky, the year
The dial is a day
Twenty-four detents, twenty-four hours. Turn the field and the light walks around you.
The three-anchor SKY table and the two drivers in _theme/arc.js
The visitor's actual sky
The sun where it really is, for wherever the reader happens to be sitting.
The same interpolation as 01
Weather that drifts through
Not a control. A condition the field is in when you arrive.
uWind and uGust are already uniforms and already animated
Four seasons, one date
The greens go yellow in October. In February the field is bleached.
The day / dusk / night anchor pattern, verbatim
The field
what lives in it and what it remembers
The grass remembers
A trail that takes half a minute to stand back up.
world.footprints is declared in the engine and never written to
Something lives here
It wanders when you are still, and follows at a distance it chooses.
The daisy heads already ride their own stems, re-pinned every frame
Cut a path through it
What you cut stays cut, because it lives in the field's own texture.
The brush is fully implemented behind TUNING.tool
Every post plants something
The archive as a garden. Turn to Engineering and see nine years of it.
stone.js, stump.js, chair.js, mug.js and five more are in git history
The writing
the words and the grass, arguing
Type that grows
The title sprouts on the same curve as the blades, and keeps the wind.
uGrow and uReveal already ease the field in over three and a half seconds
Letters that know what is behind them
Warmer where the word is in the green, cooler where it is on the sheet.
readGround() already samples the drawing buffer five times a second
The field leans away from the words
Give the headline weight, so the grass bends around it.
uBall and uTrail already do exactly this for the pointer
The chrome
navigation that belongs to the picture
The menu is the horizon
Going somewhere means turning to face it.
rig.goToScene() already picks the shorter way round
Something written at all twenty-four
Not titles, not links. Notes in a margin.
rig.onDetent() fires the instant the target changes, not on arrival
The visitor
time spent, and leaving
Idle is the feature
Thirty seconds of stillness and a bird crosses. Two minutes, something rarer.
Walk into the post
The camera dips, the field rises past you, and the article surfaces.
The camera's elevation and frustum are both live setters
